note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published on 2026-11-18. The hidden flags mark the 28 trophies PlayStation keeps hidden until unlocked (12 story trophies and 16 hidden side trophies). Every guide below is written in my own words from the trophy description and the game's mechanics; counts are taken from the description itself where it states a number.

trophies.guide: This is the last trophy you will earn, and it unlocks itself the moment the other 54 are in your collection, so treat it as a finish line rather than a task. A sensible order is the story first, then the 100% completion checklist, then the long grinds like stunts and collectibles. Save manually at the start of every chapter because missions cannot be replayed, never switch cheats on since they disable trophies, and do the first meditation in Chapter 1 before you leave Jason's house, the one spot in the game that may not come back.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy is unmissable and pops naturally within your first hour in Leonida. Follow the on-screen prompts, take your time learning the driving and shooting basics, and do not worry about medals or optional objectives on a first run. If you are new to GTA, use this mission to get comfortable with the weapon wheel, cover, and the map before the story opens up. Nothing here needs preparation, a special loadout, or a second playthrough.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 ends once you finish its final story mission, so just keep playing the golden story icons on the map and this pops on its own. Before you move on, stop at the balcony at Jason's house and meditate: that first meditation spot may be the game's only missable trophy, and Chapter 1 is the only time you are guaranteed access to it. Grab nearby collectibles and vehicles as you pass them, save manually before the chapter finale, and keep cheats off so nothing blocks your trophies later.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is where Leonida opens up properly, with new contacts, side activities, and more of the map to explore. Play through the story missions in any order the game offers, and use the quiet gaps between missions to try fishing, the shooting range, and drone races, since several trophies need those skills later. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter, keep scanning vehicles you have not driven yet, and remember that missions cannot be replayed once done.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Vice City itself takes centre stage in Chapter 3, and the trophy pops when the chapter's last story mission is complete. By now you should have both protagonists available, so use the chapter to finish any character-specific side content while you still have easy access to both. Stock up on armour and ammo before the bigger set pieces, keep a manual save at the chapter start, and sweep the new districts for meditation spots, vehicles, and collectibles as you travel between missions.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the run-up to the finale, and finishing its last mission earns this trophy. The missions here are longer and harder than anything before them, so go in with full health, armour, and a varied weapon loadout, and use cover and Combat Focus rather than rushing open ground. Before the chapter ends, check your meditation progress and your stranger strands, since post-story cleanup is easier when the list is already short. Save manually first, as always.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: The final mission is a long multi-stage set piece, so treat it like a raid: full armour, the best weapons you own, and a manual save before you start, because missions cannot be replayed. Follow the objectives step by step, use cover and your partner's positioning instead of sprinting into fire, and keep an eye on the mission's own checkpoints. Once the credits roll, this gold trophy pops, and the whole map opens up for cleanup, so any trophy you skipped can still be finished afterwards.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is an early story mission, so this trophy is unmissable: just play the story and it pops when the mission ends. It is a good early chance to practise driving smoothly under pressure, since later missions punish sloppy driving much harder. Do not stress about a perfect run; mission medals are not a trophy requirement. Finish it, then check the map for the side activities it unlocks before moving on to the next story beat.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a mid-story mission built around planning and execution, and the trophy pops when the crew gets out clean. Go in with armour and a silenced option if the approach allows it, follow the heist steps in order, and let your partners handle their roles instead of trying to do everything yourself. If a step goes wrong, use the mission checkpoint rather than restarting from scratch. Once the loot is secure and the mission wraps, the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission, so the trophy is unmissable and pops when the mission is complete. The mission leans on stealth and timing more than firepower, so move slowly, watch patrol patterns, and use cover to stay out of sight rather than fighting every enemy you see. If you are spotted, fall back and reset the encounter instead of burning through ammo. Finish the objectives, get out, and the trophy unlocks at the mission end screen.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission with a big public set piece, so expect crowds, chaos, and a lot of moving parts. Stay on the mission markers, keep your partner in sight, and use Combat Focus when the shooting starts to thin out groups quickly. The trophy pops as soon as the mission completes, so there is nothing extra to collect or do inside it. Just finish it, save afterwards, and move on to the next chapter beat.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown takes you into the airport, a restricted area where a wanted level builds fast, so plan your route in and your escape out before you start shooting. The trophy pops when the mission ends, so focus on the objectives and use vehicles and cover to break line of sight with security. Bring armour and a long-range weapon for the open tarmac sections, and remember that the airport is also the setting for a separate trophy about leaving in an unscheduled way.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is one of the biggest story missions in the game, with heavy combat and multiple phases, so come prepared: full armour, full ammo, and a manual save before you start. Use cover constantly, let Combat Focus do the work in close quarters, and do not chase enemies into open ground. The trophy pops when the operation is complete, and finishing it also unlocks later story content, so it is worth doing as soon as it appears on the map.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the real endgame: 100% completion means finishing the 35-task checklist the game tracks, covering story missions, stranger strands, stunt jumps, shooting range golds, races, robberies, collectibles, and exploration. It takes roughly 200 hours in total, so do not rush it. Work through the checklist in the pause menu, clear whole categories at a time, and save the long grinds for after the story when the full map and both characters are available. Cheats disable trophies, so keep them off for the entire run.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: A stunt counts when the game flashes the stunt prompt, and there are nearly 400 possible stunts across Leonida: stunt jumps, flights under bridges, knife-edge flights, and base jumps, with 300 needed for 100% completion. The fastest route is to chain stunt jumps with a fast bike, using the map to hop between marked jumps, and to fold bridge flights into normal travel. You do not need every stunt in the game, just 250, so skip the awkward ones and repeat the easy jumps you already know.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are nine activity types scattered around Leonida, and this trophy only asks you to try each one once, so it is a sampler, not a grind. Work through the list early: fishing, the shooting range, drone racing, arcade games, bowling, and the rest, ticking each off as you find it. The in-game activities menu shows what you have tried, and none of them needs a win or a high score, just a single attempt. Do them as you pass their locations during the story to save backtracking later.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: There are 42 Shooting Range challenges, and this silver trophy needs a gold medal in every single one, so expect to spend real time here. Learn each weapon's recoil pattern first with a few practice runs, then go for gold with steady aim rather than fast trigger pulls. Headshots and tight groupings matter more than speed in most challenges. If a challenge keeps beating you, switch weapons, rest, and come back: your scores save per challenge, so you can chip away at the list over days.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at a set of locations around Leonida, and you need a win at every one of them. Each track rewards learning the racing line: fly the first lap cautiously to memorise the gates, then push hard on the second. Upgrades and practice runs help, but the biggest gain is knowing where the tight gates are. Work through the locations region by region and tick them off as you go, since the race list in the menu shows which locations still need a win.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Twenty different races need a win here, and any race type counts: street races, off-road, boat, and air races all add to the total. The easiest wins are the early street races with a tuned car, but variety is the point, so rotate through race types and keep a different vehicle ready for each. Learn one racing line per track instead of memorising every track, brake before corners rather than in them, and use slipstreaming on the straights to pass the pack without risky moves.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is the fishing rival you meet through the fishing activity, and beating him takes more than luck: pick a rod and bait suited to the fish in that spot, watch the tension meter, and reel steadily instead of yanking. Let the fish run when the line strains, then reel hard when it slackens. Practice on ordinary catches first so the mechanics are second nature, then take Cal on when you are confident. The trophy pops the moment you out-fish him in the challenge.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Any arcade cabinet in Leonida will do: walk up, start a game, and play it through to the end. Arcade games here are short, score-based affairs, so pick one with simple controls on your first attempt and learn its patterns rather than mashing buttons. You do not need a high score or a leaderboard place, just a completed run. Arcades are marked on the map, and finishing one game also counts toward trying the activity types for the Master of None trophy.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's final mission closes out his whole storyline, so the trophy pops when that last mission ends. Side-character finales tend to be harder than their earlier missions, so bring armour, ammo, and a manual save before you start. Andy's missions are Lucia-only, so make sure you are playing as the right character before you travel to the marker. Finish the mission, watch the storyline wrap up, and the trophy unlocks at the end screen.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's final mission is the end of his strand, and it is usually a tense, combat-heavy send-off. Go in prepared with a full loadout and use the mission's cover and checkpoints rather than rushing. The trophy is story-gated, so it pops automatically when the mission completes; there is nothing hidden to find inside it. Once it is done, Kenton's strand is closed for good, so enjoy the payoff and move on to the next strand.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's final mission wraps up his storyline, and like the other side finales it is a proper mission, not a quick errand. Expect a longer drive, a set piece, and a fight at the end, so stock up before you set out and save manually at the start. The trophy pops at the mission end screen. If you have been doing Billy's missions as they appear, this one unlocks naturally; if not, check the map for his icon and clear his earlier missions first.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers and Freaks strands are the odd jobs and weird encounters scattered across Leonida, and eight full strands are needed here. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished strands do not help: pick a stranger, follow their missions to the end, then move to the next. Some strands only appear after story progress or with a specific character, so check the map regularly and clear them as they appear rather than leaving them all for the post-game.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's final mission closes his strand, so the trophy pops when it ends. Randy's missions lean into the seedier side of Leonida, with deals and double-crosses, so expect a fight or a chase in the finale. Bring a fast car and full armour, save before you start, and follow the mission markers rather than improvising. Once the last objective is done, the strand is complete and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's final mission is the last step in his storyline, and Tyrone's missions are Jason-only, so switch to Jason before heading to the marker. The finale is a proper mission with combat and driving, so arrive with armour and a good vehicle. The trophy unlocks when the mission completes. If Tyrone's icon is not on the map yet, keep playing the story: his strand opens up as the chapters progress.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida, and this is the one trophy in the game that may be missable: the first spot is the balcony at Jason's house, and you can only reach it during Chapter 1, so meditate there before the chapter ends. After that, spots unlock as the story progresses, with the last ones needing both characters after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break. Visit each spot, meditate until the prompt completes, and track your count in the menu so no spot is left behind. Do this one early and the rest is a relaxed tour.
trophies.missable_note: Meditate at the balcony at Jason's house during Chapter 1 — that spot may not be reachable later. The remaining spots unlock through the story; the last ones need both characters after Coffee Break in Chapter 2.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret sends you after a unique animal, a one-of-a-kind hunt that needs tracking rather than firepower. Follow the clues and tracks to the animal's territory, approach downwind and quietly, and use a scoped weapon for a clean shot rather than spraying bullets. The animal will flee if spooked, so save before the final approach and be patient. Once the hunt is complete and you report back to Bret, the trophy pops. Bret's strand is Jason-only, so play as Jason for this one.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Collectible card sets are hidden all over Leonida, and three complete sets are needed here. Cards are tucked into shops, houses, and odd corners, so check every interior you enter and use the collectible tracker to see which sets are close to complete. Trade duplicates with other players' listings or swap with friends if you are missing one stubborn card, and focus on one set at a time so your collection fills evenly instead of scattering across all of them.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It means tagging 100 locations with the in-game phone app, and the fastest way is to treat it like a sightseeing tour: open the app at every landmark, viewpoint, and district sign you pass, and work region by region so nothing is missed. The app shows your count, so you can see how far along you are. Fold the tagging into normal travel and story missions instead of grinding it in one sitting, and the hundred comes naturally before the endgame.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Fifty challenges is a big number, but challenges are the small feats the game tracks everywhere: driving, shooting, flying, and exploring all have their own lists, with 80 challenges in total. Pick the easy ones first, such as distance driven and enemies taken down, and let the harder ones accumulate as you play. The challenge menu shows your progress per category, so clear whole categories at a time and leave the awkward ones until you have the right vehicle or weapon for them.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: You need a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then you have to lose the cops and escape. The trick is to earn the stars in a quiet area with a fast car nearby: cause chaos until the fourth star appears, then break line of sight, switch vehicles if you can, and hide until the stars blink and fade. Your partner must still be with you when the heat dies, so do not abandon them mid-chase. A rural road with plenty of side streets works better than downtown.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner without ever losing your wanted level, which means the whole run is one continuous crime spree. Plan a route with three close shops, hit them fast, and keep moving between them so the cops never catch up. A fast getaway car parked outside each shop helps, and your partner needs to stay with you for all three robberies. If the wanted level drops to zero mid-run, the chain breaks and you start over, so keep the pressure on.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discovering a vehicle means driving it for the first time, and 100 different vehicles are needed here. The vehicle list in the menu shows what you have found and what is still missing. Scan traffic as you drive, steal anything unusual you spot, and visit car parks, dealerships, and docks where rare models spawn. Story missions hand you several unique vehicles for free, and the rest appear in traffic or at specific locations, so keep an eye out rather than grinding one spot.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus slows time and lets you line up shots, and this trophy needs five enemies downed in a single use. Find a group of enemies in an open area, trigger Combat Focus when they are clustered, and aim for headshots to drop them fast before the meter runs out. A mission with a big firefight is the best place to try, since enemies keep coming to you. If you only get three or four, reload the checkpoint and try again with better positioning.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the airport, and an unscheduled departure means leaving it in a way the airport did not plan: steal a plane and take off without clearance. Get onto the tarmac, grab a plane, and get airborne before security closes in, then fly clear of the airport airspace. A wanted level is almost guaranteed, so lose it after you are safely away. The airport is restricted, so a fast approach and a quicker takeoff matter more than a firefight on the runway.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the military tanks that show up when your wanted level gets very high, and this trophy is about surviving the encounter with them, hot as it gets. Get to five stars in an open area, keep moving so the tank cannon cannot track you, and use sticky bombs or heavy weapons if you want to fight back. Honestly, the safest approach is to stay mobile, use cover and alleyways, and let the chaos play out until the trophy pops. Bring armour and a fast vehicle.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: A jewelry store robbery without being detected means a clean, quiet job: case the store first, learn the guard patrols and camera positions, and move in with a silenced approach. Take down guards quietly, grab the goods, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the trophy fails for that attempt, so restart from a save rather than fighting your way out. Patience and planning beat firepower here, and a night-time attempt gives you more shadows to work with.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Five bank vaults, five clean escapes: each vault is a full robbery with its own planning, entry, and getaway, so treat every one as a mini-heist. Learn the vault layout, bring a crew-friendly loadout, and have a fast car waiting outside for the escape. The wanted level after a vault job is heavy, so plan your escape route before you go in, use tunnels and back streets, and do not stop to fight. Complete all five and the silver trophy pops.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks are the slow, tough vans that carry cash around Leonida, and this trophy asks you to rob one and escape. Ram it or block it until it stops, crack it open with explosives or a heavy weapon, grab the cash, and get out before the police response builds. A quiet road outside the city is a better ambush spot than downtown, and a fast car parked nearby makes the escape much easier. Once you are clear of the wanted level, the trophy pops.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Exploring all of Leonida means visiting every district and region on the map, from Vice City's beaches to the swamps and small towns inland. The map tracks your progress, so open it regularly to see which areas are still dark and drive through them. Fly or drive the borders of each region to make sure the game registers the visit, and combine the tour with collectibles, meditation spots, and vehicle hunting so the trip does double duty. No single area is hard to reach; it just takes time.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Each gang in Leonida runs illegal operations, and this trophy needs you to rob one operation belonging to every gang. That means learning which gang controls which turf, finding their operation, and hitting it cleanly. Operations are marked once you discover them, and each one plays differently, so scout before you strike. Work through the gangs one at a time and tick them off the list, and expect a fight at every operation, so go in armed and ready.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is the classic Vice City waterfront, and this trophy is as simple as it sounds: order a cocktail at a bar with a view of the ocean and enjoy it. Head to a beachfront bar in the evening, sit where you can see the water, and order the drink from the menu. There is no trick and no time limit, just a quiet moment in the game. It is best done during a break between missions, and it pairs nicely with a stroll down the beach afterwards.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: This one is a nod to the classic GTA showroom smash: drive into a vehicle showroom and power your way out through the glass in style. Pick a showroom with a big front window, build up speed outside, and drive straight through, smashing the glass and scattering the display cars. A fast, heavy car works best, and the chaos is the point, so do not worry about the damage bill. The trophy pops once you have made your exit in suitably dramatic fashion.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The Kolt and Associates bowling alley hides a trophy behind its lanes, and the guides read it as a heist-flavoured job: steal three valuables from inside the alley rather than simply bowling a game. Case the place first, spot the valuables and the staff patrols, then lift all three without being caught. If you are spotted, leave and try again. The alley itself is worth a visit anyway, and the trophy pops once the third valuable is in your pocket.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal is a deliberately vague description, and the community reads it as a social-media-flavoured feat: build your in-game following or partnership profile until it hits the threshold the game wants. Post, share, and complete the social activities that raise your profile, and check the relevant menu to see your progress. It is a slow burn rather than a single action, so fold it into normal play and let the numbers climb over the course of the story.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse: this trophy tracks the decisions you make across the story and the open world. There is no single right answer, so just play naturally, take the choices that feel right for your run, and let the count build up over time. Dialogue options, mission decisions, and side-activity choices all feed into it. You cannot miss it by choosing wrong, because the game counts the act of choosing, not the outcome, so keep playing and it pops on its own.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: this trophy is about succeeding on a retry, so it pops when you pull off something after failing it once. The easiest way is to find a small challenge or stunt you can fail safely, such as a stunt jump you deliberately miss, then land it cleanly on the second attempt. The game tracks attempts, so a genuine second try is what counts. Do not overthink it; most players earn this one naturally during a long playthrough without ever trying.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? This trophy is for witnessing one of Leonida's strangest sights, the kind of odd event that makes you stop and stare. Strange encounters appear at specific places and times, often at night or in remote spots, so explore the weird corners of the map and keep your eyes open. The game gives no marker for it, so curiosity is the method: visit the odd locations, wait a while, and the moment will find you. It pops the instant the event plays out.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by means knocking people off their bikes with a melee weapon while you drive past, and the guides read the real requirement as ten pedestrians knocked off a bike within sixty seconds. Find a busy stretch of road, grab a fast bike, and line up your swings as you pass riders. Timing matters more than speed: swing just as you draw level. Chain the hits quickly and the trophy pops once the tenth rider goes down inside the minute.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are the dirty cash you earn from certain jobs, and laundering $250,000 of them through your contacts is a slow, steady grind. Hand the bills to your contacts whenever you have them rather than letting them pile up, and keep doing jobs that pay in marked bills so the supply never dries up. The game tracks the laundered total, so check your progress regularly. There is no shortcut: it is a matter of volume, and the total builds up naturally across the story.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spending $100,000 across all shops sounds like a lot until you realise how fast it adds up: weapons, ammo, clothes, cars, and property upgrades all count. Buy the gear you actually need as you play, upgrade your vehicles, and keep a wardrobe that suits both characters. The counter tracks every dollar spent in any shop, so there is no single big purchase required. By the end of the story, most players are most of the way there without even trying.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Garage properties are the safehouses and storage spaces you can buy around Leonida, and this trophy needs you to own all of them. Each garage costs money and holds a different set of vehicles, so buy them as your cash allows, starting with the ones near the areas you visit most. The property menu shows which ones you still need. Once the last garage is yours, the trophy pops, and you will have parking for every vehicle in your collection.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles you find around Leonida, and ten registrations are needed here. Open the app whenever you drive something new, snap the vehicle, and register it. The app tracks your count, so you can see how close you are. Rare and unusual vehicles are worth seeking out, but ordinary traffic counts too, so register everything you drive during normal play and the ten will come quickly.
trophies.name: On the Spot
